tagline: Over a hand-cranked swing bridge and up to the Post Road.
intro: The scenic run of Route 136 begins on the Saugatuck River Bridge at Saugatuck, a name from the Paugussett meaning the mouth of the tidal river, and goes a little under two miles north to the Post Road in Westport.

Westport was a seaport from the start. For some decades after its incorporation in 1835 it was the leading onion-growing center in the country, and a shipping center partly to carry the onions to market, until blight ended the trade. Boats mattered enough that the bridge was built to swing open and let them through.

moments.title: Saugatuck River Bridge
moments.text: The hand-cranked wrought-iron swing span of 1884 replaced a wooden bridge of 1869 that shipworms had made nearly impassable before the town finished paying for it.

moments.title: Westport Village
moments.text: The route ends at the town center on the Post Road, where from about 1910 artists and writers, F. Scott Fitzgerald among them, came to live clear of the commute.
